issue_text: I’m Maya Chen. Please pull up round-trip reservation C4C633 first. I want to cancel it because my plans changed, but before you do anything, confirm whether the entire trip is eligible for cancellation and give me the full itinerary, both passengers, any insurance on the booking, the total baggage count, the payment method used, and exactly how the refund would work.
summary: An airline session for Maya Chen (silver tier) handling cancellations, a compensation request, a flight change, two new bookings, and a cabin upgrade. T1 reviews round-trip C4C633 and correctly rules it ineligible for a 'change of plans' cancellation; T2 lists the full account (five confirmed reservations). T3–T4 review the Vegas booking EC4C1C and deny a compensation request, correctly reasoning that insurance on a different reservation (C4C633) or silver status does not entitle this economy booking to compensation absent a disruption (trap_0, handled well). T5–T8 change reservation A2CBB0 to a cheaper nearby flight (+$129) with a confirm-before-execute preview. T9–T11 book new SEA→SFO and JFK→MIA economy trips. T12 is the key failure: asked to upgrade A2CBB0 to business, the agent quotes the 'cabin must remain the same across all flights' modification policy, then rationalizes it away ('no flights have been flown yet') and performs the upgrade (+$260). The agent's booking-specific policy recall is strong throughout, but the cabin-upgrade rule is recalled and then overridden — the one real policy miss of the run.
